variants.name: A-watercolor-ink
variants.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit the supplied Blender render of the existing Wick Spirit game character into a polished nonphotorealistic 3D-to-2D shading concept. This is the SAME character, not a redesign. Preserve EXACTLY the reference silhouette, huge flame-shaped head with its existing pointed tufts, tiny body, short arms and feet, oval dark eyes, small mouth, chest flame emblem, pose, three-quarter orthographic camera, full-body framing and relative scale. Preserve the plain dark slate-gray background and the same direction of key light. Only change how the surface, shadows, contours and emission are drawn. Make it convincingly look like a 2D illustrated game sprite rather than a softly lit 3D clay toy. Keep the original ivory, muted blue-gray and subtle warm gold palette. No new accessories, no scene, no different anatomy, no text or logos. STYLE A: hand-inked watercolor storybook cel shading. Broad translucent ivory watercolor washes, visible pigment granulation within large shapes, just TWO broad blue-gray shadow values, softly irregular pigment edges, fine broken warm charcoal contour around silhouette and selected facial details. Flatten round cheeks and torso shading into intentional graphic shapes. Chest glow is a tiny soft pale gold accent. Most faithful to an artistic watercolor puzzle-game world. No realistic smooth gradient modeling.
